messages:
Maya: thinking about runtime config/feature flags for routing policies. Proposal: evaluate flags in the API gateway/proxy layer (fast, shared cache) instead of inside model runtime. pros/cons?

Kevin: proxy eval reduces per-worker duplication and keeps hot path cheap. also easier to audit. downside: proxy needs model-aware logic for fallbacks.

Priya: +1 on observability. if proxy decides routing, we must emit per-request decision tags so logs/trace show which variant served it.

Jonah: concern: some flags depend on KV cache state (e.g., session size or user context) that only runtime has. how do we keep consistent semantics without blocking?

Amanda: pattern idea: proxy is the primary decision point. runtime can call a tiny decision endpoint (bounded timeout) if it needs extra context. contract: proxy returns header X-RWD-Variant and X-RWD-Group, runtime honors header if present. if absent or timeout -> runtime falls back to local stable variant. non-blocking.

Maya: fallback semantics must be explicit in the RFC. kill-switch required. runtime must never block request > fallback timeout.

Priya: rollout strategy: percent-based + rule sets. example rule payload we discussed: 
```
{
  "flag": "model_routing_v2",
  "rules": [
    {"type":"percent","value":20},
    {"type":"allowlist","users":["acct:123"]}
  ],
  "timeout_ms": 30
}
```
(note: this is the decision-service input, not an internal object)

Kevin: timeout important. if decision-service times out, runtime must default to the stable variant, not the candidate. we should make that explicit default.

Jonah: telemetry we need on rollouts/SLOs: error_rate, p95_latency, token_cost_delta, quality_regression_score. sample PromQLs for dashboards: 
```
sum(rate(rwd_request_errors[5m])) by (variant)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(rwd_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,variant))
```
Also track decision_service_latency_ms and decision_cache_hit_ratio.

Amanda: UX: console should let you create canaries by percent, by customer (API key), by region. In the rollout view show live percent, recent error delta, and a one-click rollback.

Maya: propose automated rollback triggers: error_rate > 2x baseline OR p95 latency regression > 100ms sustained for 10m -> auto rollback + page the oncall. Need to store baseline per-variant.

Priya: config propagation: we can accept eventual consistency generally, but need atomic multi-flag rollouts. proposal: group-id/versioned rollout groups. decision payload includes group_id and group_version. runtime will only apply if group_version >= local_group_version to avoid partial application.

Kevin: implement group-id semantics in the proxy. add a header X-RWD-Group and X-RWD-Group-Version. runtime will verify and log if mismatch.

Jonah: operational note: decision logs must be sampled (1-5%) to avoid high cardinality. also expose metrics for decision_cache_hits/misses and proxy_eval_rate.

Maya: CLI example for quick testing: 
```
rwdctl flags set model_routing_v2 --percent=50 --group=canary-2026-03
```

deploy-bot: flag "model_routing_v2" set to 50% (group=canary-2026-03) by Maya

Amanda: security question for Private (VPC/on-prem): how to secure decision channel between proxy and runtime? mTLS + short-lived signed tokens + nonce replay protection.

Kevin: agree. also require RBAC on who can create rollout groups. sign group metadata.

Priya: compliance: we need audit logs for all flag changes and rollbacks. store who/why/timestamp and link to console event. retention policy? 1 year default, longer for enterprise.

Maya: next steps: 1) spec proxy decision API + header contract, 2) telemetry metrics list + dashboards, 3) console canary UX mock + rollback flow, 4) implement group-id semantics and timeout defaults. volunteers?

Kevin: I can own the proxy API doc.

Priya: I'll draft telemetry + dashboard panels.

Jonah: I'll prototype runtime header honoring and a non-blocking timeout.

Amanda: I'll mock console canary view and rollback button wired to API.

Maya: I'll write the rollout policy RFC with auto-rollback thresholds and baseline definitions. thanks! :tada:
